programs.title: KOL traffic secrets: the power to drive change #GlobalSouthNextGen Behind the scenes
programs.desc: How do creators build traffic on social media? How can that influence spark real changes in society? In a cozy siheyuan, the iconic Beijing courtyard, another episode of #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions brings together two KOLs who open up about their journeys, their strategies, and the impact from their content. Click into the Behind the Scenes video to find out more!

programs.title: China's ocean economy at a turning point
programs.desc: Since elevating the goal of becoming a "maritime power" in 2012, China has made significant progress. What are the most eye-catching achievements? As the focus shifts from speed to quality, how could China's AI and digital tech edge help reshape the country's traditional maritime sectors? And in a system where a few countries still hold technological and narrative dominance, how can China gain a greater voice in rule-setting through global cooperation? Host TU Yun joins Yan Yan, a senior research fellow with the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, Qu Qiang, a professor and fellow of the Belt and Road Research Center at Minzu University of China, and Warwick Powell, an adjunct professor at Queensland University of Technology, to navigate the opportunities, challenges, and what lies beneath the surface.

programs.title: BizTalk: China-US economic & trade watch
programs.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programs.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programs.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programs.title: The green bridge between China & US
programs.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programs.title: China-US: The efficiency advantage
programs.desc: The iPhone in your pocket? A global masterpiece. Apple's supply chain spans the world, with America's design expertise meeting China's manufacturing strength. Precision, speed and scale turn bold ideas into products in your hands. And this goes beyond Apple: cooperation across borders can drive innovation and growth. When the world's two biggest economies click, everyone benefits.

programs.title: RAZOR: The Looming Threat of Super AI
programs.desc: The head of AI company Anthropic has called for the pace of development of artificial intelligence models to slow down and to be closely monitored. Neil Cairns speaks to MIT professor and physicist Max Tegmark about the looming threat posed to the human race by the unrestricted development of Artificial Intelligence. In 2014, Max founded the Future Life Institute which campaigns for AI safety and pushes for regulations to be imposed on companies developing AI so as to stop the creation of Artificial General Intelligence and Super Intelligence, two specific forms of AI which could see human beings handing over power to machines, making them our descendants.

programs.title: RAZOR: AI Supercomputer
programs.desc: This episode, Razor explores Isambard AI, the UK's new AI supercomputer, and how advanced computing is accelerating scientific research. Featuring interviews with researchers from Bristol Centre for Supercomputing, the program examines how AI and supercomputing are being used to study diseases, analyze complex biological data, and speed up discoveries in medicine and life sciences. Scientists say the platform can dramatically reduce the time needed for research, opening new possibilities for drug development and scientific innovation while highlighting the growing importance of AI infrastructure in the future of science.

programs.title: Integration and Empowerment - A New Paradigm of Sino-German Cooperation Driven by Technological Innovation
programs.desc: For the first time, the Sino-German Forum on Cooperation and Development of New Energy Vehicles and the VDA Round Table of Presidents/CEOs of German Suppliers in China will be jointly held as a combined event during the World New Energy Vehicle Congress (WNEVC). The forum brings together industry leaders to explore collaborative development in the NEV sector, covering topics such as industry trends, innovation, policy frameworks, and international cooperation.

programs.title: Jobs 2.0: Who's teaching the robots to work?
programs.desc: As robots gradually move from research labs into real-world tasks, a key question emerges: how do machines learn to handle complex, delicate work? At a Beijing robotics company, engineers are hand-training robotic hands, translating human experience into digital skills that can be replicated at scale. CGTN's Yang Xinmeng explores this emerging profession, speaking with the people who teach machines to cook, care, and manipulate objects with precision. Their work offers a rare glimpse into the intersection of human ingenuity and artificial intelligence – and into the ways humans and robots may collaborate in everyday life.

programs.title: Jobs 2.0: From trash to treasure
programs.desc: Jiao Jianwei is a senior engineer at the Longgang Energy Eco-Park inShenzhen. Every day, the facility processes 5,000 tonnes of waste, burning it togenerate electricity that powers millions of homes. The leftover ash is alsoturned into eco-bricks, used to pave city roads. From landfills to incineration,China has transformed its waste industry with advanced technologies. Today,the country operates more than 1,000 waste-to-energy plants – nearly half theworld's total. With national goals like "carbon neutrality" and "zero-wastecities" taking shape, engineers like Jiao are turning trash into treasure.

programs.title: Meet China: Flying into the Future, Growing a Greener City, and Connecting Business to the World
programs.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how the future is taking shape across different corners of China and beyond. From Guangzhou's rising low-altitude economy powered by electric flying cars, to Xiamen's practical path toward zero-carbon urban life, we see how innovation is changing the way people live and cities grow. We also step into China's booming livestream shopping culture, where commerce becomes community, and travel to Malaysia's rice fields, where Chinese agricultural expertise is helping improve harvests and food security. This episode reveals how technology, industry and creativity are turning bold ideas into everyday reality.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Malaysia's rice has a secret superpower
programs.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Chinese ratoon rice technology is now being applied to lift yields and enhance food security—unlocking new potential for tropical farming. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programs.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programs.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programs.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programs.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programs.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programs.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programs.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programs.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programs.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programs.title: KOLs and other ways to connect cultures
programs.desc: In what ways can KOLs better use their power in an age where a single video can reach millions? Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions, and check out the stories of two KOLs from Ghana and Indonesia who use their creativity, empathy, and the shared desire to make people understand each other a little better.
